title.zh: 卷一百十七 志第七十 禮二十
title.raw: 卷一百十七 志第七十 禮二十 Volume 117 Treatises 70: Rites 20

sentences.zh: 禮二十

translations.literal: Rites Twenty
translations.idiomatic: Rites 20

sentences.zh: （賓禮二）〉

translations.literal: (Guest Rites II))
translations.idiomatic: Guest Rites II

sentences.zh: ○入閣儀明堂聽政儀肆赦儀附皇太后垂簾儀皇太子正至受賀儀皇太子與百官師保相見儀

translations.literal: ○ Entering-the-Palace-Hall Rite; Hall of Brightness Audience Rite; General Amnesty Rite; appended: Empress Dowager Behind-the-Curtain Rite; Crown Prince Winter Solstice Reception-of-Congratulations Rite; Crown Prince Meeting Officials, Tutors, and Protectors Rite
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Palace Hall; audience at the Hall of Brightness; general amnesty; the empress dowager behind the curtain; the crown prince receiving congratulations at the winter solstice; and the crown prince meeting officials with his tutors and protectors

sentences.zh: 入閣儀。

translations.literal: The Entering-the-Palace-Hall Rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Entering-the-Palace-Hall Ceremony

sentences.zh: 唐制：天子日御正衙以見群臣，必立仗。

translations.literal: Tang regulation: the Son of Heaven daily held court in the main audience hall to see the ministers, and guard formations were always posted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, the emperor held daily audience in the main hall and always posted ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 朔望薦食陵寢，不能臨前殿，則御便殿，乃自正衙喚仗由宣政兩門而入，是謂東、西上閣門，群臣俟於正衙者因隨以入，故謂之入閣。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month, when offering food at the imperial tombs, if he could not attend the front hall, he would hold court in the side hall; then from the main audience hall he summoned the guard formation to enter through the two gates of Xuanzheng—called the eastern and western upper palace-gate doors—and the ministers waiting in the main audience hall followed in; hence it was called entering the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moon days, when the emperor made tomb offerings and could not attend the front hall, he held court in a side hall instead. Guards summoned from the main hall entered through the eastern and western upper gates of the Xuanzheng Palace, and officials waiting there followed them in—hence the name “entering the palace hall.”

sentences.zh: 五代以來，正衙既廢，而入閣亦希闊不講，宋復行之。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward, the main audience hall was abolished, and entering the palace hall was also rare and no longer observed; Song restored the practice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Five Dynasties the main audience hall fell out of use and the inner-hall ceremony was rarely performed; the Song revived it.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年四月朔，常服通天冠、絳紗袍，御崇元殿視朝，設金吾仗衛，群臣入閣。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month of the fourth year of Qiande, in ordinary dress with the open-through-the-heavens cap and crimson gauze robe, he held court at the Hall of August Origin, set out the Golden Crow guard formation, and the ministers entered the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month of Qiande 4, Taizu held court at the Hall of August Origin in everyday dress with the open crown and crimson gauze robe, posted the Golden Crow guard, and received ministers in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗淳化二年十一月，詔以十二月朔御文德殿入閣，令史館修撰楊徽之、張洎定為新儀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Chunhua under Taizong, an edict ordered that on the first day of the twelfth month he should hold the entering-the-palace-hall audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue, and ordered Hanlin compilers Yang Huizhi and Zhang Ji to fix the new rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Chunhua 2, Taizong decreed an inner-hall audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue on the first day of the twelfth month and charged Yang Huizhi and Zhang Ji of the Historiography Institute to draft new protocol.

sentences.zh: 前一日，有司供帳於文德殿

translations.literal: On the day before, the responsible offices supplied the furnishings at the Hall of Civil Virtue
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the responsible offices set up the Hall of Civil Virtue

sentences.zh: （宋初曰「文明」）〉

translations.literal: (at the beginning of Song it was called “Civilization”))
translations.idiomatic: called “Civilization” in early Song

sentences.zh: 是日既明，先列文武官於殿庭之東西，百官、軍校、行軍副使等序班於正衙門外屏南階下；

translations.literal: When that day had grown light, civil and military officials were first arrayed east and west in the palace courtyard; all officials, military officers, and deputy expedition commanders lined up in order on the southern steps below the screen outside the main audience gate;
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, civil and military officials formed ranks east and west in the courtyard, while other officials, military officers, and deputy expedition commanders lined up on the southern steps outside the screen before the main audience gate;

sentences.zh: 次御史中丞、三院御史序立，中丞獨穿金吾班過揖兩班，一揖歸本位；

translations.literal: next the vice censor-in-chief and censors of the three bureaus took their places in order; the vice censor alone passed through the Golden Crow formation and bowed to both lines, one bow, then returned to his place;
translations.idiomatic: next the vice censor-in-chief and censors of the three bureaus took position; the vice censor alone passed through the Golden Crow guard line, bowed once to each side, and returned to his place;

sentences.zh: 次監察御史兩員監閣，於正衙門外屏北階上北面立；

translations.literal: next two investigating censors supervised the palace hall, standing facing north on the northern steps of the screen outside the main audience gate;
translations.idiomatic: next two investigating censors took up supervision of the hall, standing on the northern steps outside the screen, facing north;

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、文明翰林樞密直學士、兩省官分班立；

translations.literal: next officials of the Secretariat, Chancellery, Civilization Hall, Hanlin Academy, Privy Council academicians, and the two provinces lined up in separate formations;
translations.idiomatic: next Secretariat, Chancellery, Hanlin, Privy Council, and two-province officials formed separate lines;

sentences.zh: 次司天奏辰刻；

translations.literal: next the Bureau of Astronomy reported the hour;
translations.idiomatic: next the Bureau of Astronomy announced the hour;

sentences.zh: 次閣門版奏班齊。

translations.literal: next the Palace Gate office reported on the tally board that the formations were complete.
translations.idiomatic: next the Palace Gate office reported that all formations were in place.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服靴袍乘輦，至長春殿駐輦，樞密使以下奏謁，前導至文德殿。

translations.literal: The emperor, wearing boots and robe and riding the palanquin, halted the palanquin at the Hall of Everlasting Spring; the privy councilor and those below reported for audience, then led the way to the Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in boots and robe, rode the palanquin to the Hall of Everlasting Spring, where the privy councilor and others presented themselves; escorts then led him to the Hall of Civil Virtue.

sentences.zh: 殿上承旨索扇，卷簾。

translations.literal: On the hall, the recipient of edicts called for fans; the curtains were rolled up.
translations.idiomatic: On the dais the edict recipient called for fans, and the curtains were raised.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升位，扇卻，儀鸞使焚香；

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the throne; the fans were withdrawn; the ceremonial guard commissioner burned incense;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the throne; fans were withdrawn and the ceremonial guard commissioner burned incense;

sentences.zh: 次文武官等拜；

translations.literal: next civil and military officials and others bowed;
translations.idiomatic: next civil and military officials bowed;

sentences.zh: 次司天雞唱；

translations.literal: next the Bureau of Astronomy crowed like a cock;
translations.idiomatic: next the Bureau of Astronomy announced the hour with the cock call;

sentences.zh: 次閣門勘契；

translations.literal: next the Palace Gate office verified the tally;
translations.idiomatic: next the Palace Gate office verified the tally tokens;

sentences.zh: 次閣門使承旨呼四色官喚仗，南班有辭謝者再拜先退，中書、門下班對揖，序立正衙門外屏北階上；

translations.literal: next the palace gate commissioner, receiving the edict, called the four-color officers to summon the guard formation; those of the southern formation who had leave to decline bowed twice and withdrew first; the Secretariat and Chancellery formations bowed to each other in pairs and lined up in order on the northern steps of the screen outside the main audience gate;
translations.idiomatic: next the gate commissioner, on imperial order, had the four-color officers summon the guard; southern-line officials with leave to decline bowed twice and withdrew; Secretariat and Chancellery lines exchanged paired bows and took position on the northern steps outside the screen;

sentences.zh: 次翰林學士、兩省官、中丞、侍御史序立；

translations.literal: next Hanlin academicians, two-province officials, the vice censor, and attendant censors took their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: next Hanlin academicians, two-province officials, the vice censor, and attendant censors took position;

sentences.zh: 次金吾將軍押細仗入正衙門後，橫行拜訖，分行上黃道，仗隨入，金吾將軍至龍墀分班揖訖，序立；

translations.literal: next the Golden Crow general escorted the detailed guard formation in behind the main audience gate; after bowing while crossing, they split and ascended the yellow path, the guard following in; the Golden Crow general reached the dragon terrace, bowed in separate formations, then lined up in order;
translations.idiomatic: next the Golden Crow general led the detailed guard through the main gate; after a crosswise bow they split ranks, ascended the yellow path with the guard following, and at the dragon terrace bowed by formation before taking position;

sentences.zh: 次吏部、兵部侍郎執文武班簿入，對揖立；

translations.literal: next the vice ministers of Personnel and War, holding the civil and military roster books, entered, bowed to each other in pairs, and stood;
translations.idiomatic: next the vice ministers of Personnel and War entered with the civil and military rosters, exchanged paired bows, and stood;

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、學士、兩省、御史台官入，北面拜訖，上黃道，將至午階，𣀃𣀃鞾急趨赴丹墀，彈奏御史至吏部侍郎南便落黃道，急趨就位；

translations.literal: next Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, two provinces, and Censorate officials entered, bowed facing north, then ascended the yellow path; as they neared the noon steps they stamped their boots twice and hurried to the cinnabar terrace; the impeachment censor to the vice minister of Personnel turned south at the edge, left the yellow path, and hurried to take position;
translations.idiomatic: next Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, two-province, and Censorate officials entered and bowed northward, then mounted the yellow path; nearing the central steps they stamped their boots and hurried to the cinnabar terrace; the impeachment censor and others south of the Personnel vice minister left the path and rushed to their places;

sentences.zh: 起居郎、舍人至兵部、吏部侍郎後，急趨而進，飛至香案前，皆揖訖序立；

translations.literal: the attendance recorder and palace secretaries, reaching behind the War and Personnel vice ministers, hurried forward, flew to the incense table, all bowed, then lined up in order;
translations.idiomatic: the attendance recorder and palace secretaries, following the War and Personnel vice ministers, hurried forward to the incense table, bowed, and took position;

sentences.zh: 次金吾大將軍先對揖並鞠躬，𣀃鞾行至折方石位又對揖，北行至奏事石位鞠躬，一員奏軍國內外平安，倒行就位；

translations.literal: next the Golden Crow grand general first bowed in pairs and bent at the waist, stamped his boots and walked to the square-turning stone and again bowed in pairs, walked north to the memorial stone and bowed; one officer reported that within and without the army and state all was secure, then walked backward to take position;
translations.idiomatic: next the Golden Crow grand general exchanged paired bows and bent low, stamped his boots and advanced to the turning stone for another paired bow, then north to the memorial stone to bow; one officer reported that the realm was at peace, then backed to his place;

sentences.zh: 次引文武班就位，揖訖，鞠躬，𣀃鞾急趨入沙墀；

translations.literal: next the civil and military formations were led to their places; when bows were finished they bent, stamped their boots, and hurried into the sand terrace;
translations.idiomatic: next civil and military ranks were led in; after bowing they bent low, stamped their boots, and hurried onto the sand terrace;

sentences.zh: 次引侍從班橫行，宰相祝月起居畢，分班序立；

translations.literal: next the attendant formation was led across; when the chief councilor had finished the monthly congratulatory attendance, they split into formations and lined up in order;
translations.idiomatic: next the attendant line crossed; after the chief councilor offered the monthly congratulations, ranks split and took position;

sentences.zh: 文武兩班出，序立於衙門外。

translations.literal: The civil and military two formations went out and lined up in order outside the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: Both civil and military formations then filed out and lined up beyond the yamen gate.

sentences.zh: 刑法、待制官赴監奏位，中書、門下夾香案侍立，兩省、御史台官、學士、兵部吏部侍郎、金吾將軍、監閣御史並相次出，就衙門外立

translations.literal: Penal-law and awaiting-edict officials went to the supervisory memorial position; Secretariat and Chancellery stood attending on either side of the incense table; two-province, Censorate, academician, War and Personnel vice ministers, Golden Crow general, and supervising censors all went out in succession and stood outside the yamen gate
translations.idiomatic: Penal-law and awaiting-edict officials took the supervisory memorial post; Secretariat and Chancellery stood flanking the incense table; two-province, Censorate, Hanlin, War and Personnel vice ministers, Golden Crow general, and supervising censors filed out in turn to stand outside the gate

sentences.zh: （惟學士立門側北候宰相）〉

translations.literal: (only academicians stood north of the gate side awaiting the chief councilor))
translations.idiomatic: academicians alone waited north of the gate for the chief councilor

sentences.zh: 中書、門下詣香案前奏曰：“中書公事，臣等已具奏聞。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery went before the incense table and reported: “Secretariat business—your subjects have already fully reported it.”
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery advanced to the incense table and said, “Your servants have already reported Secretariat business in full.”

sentences.zh: ”訖，乃退，揖殿出。

translations.literal: When finished, they withdrew, bowed toward the hall, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: When done, they withdrew, bowed toward the hall, and left.

sentences.zh: 次刑法官、待制官各奏事，並宣徽使答訖，乃出就班。

translations.literal: next penal-law officials and awaiting-edict officials each reported business, and the Palace Domestic commissioner answered; when finished, they went out to join their formations.
translations.idiomatic: Next penal-law and awaiting-edict officials each presented business, the Palace Domestic commissioner replied, and they returned to formation.

sentences.zh: 次彈奏官、左右史出。

translations.literal: next the impeachment officer and left and right recorders went out.
translations.idiomatic: Next the impeachment officer and left and right recorders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 閣內失儀者，彈糾如式。

translations.literal: Those who breached decorum within the palace hall were impeached according to the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: Breach of decorum inside the hall was impeached according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 彈奏官失儀，起居郎糾之；

translations.literal: If the impeachment officer breached decorum, the attendance recorder corrected him;
translations.idiomatic: If the impeachment officer erred, the attendance recorder corrected him;

sentences.zh: 起居郎失儀，閣門使糾之；

translations.literal: if the attendance recorder breached decorum, the palace gate commissioner corrected him;
translations.idiomatic: if the attendance recorder erred, the gate commissioner corrected him;

sentences.zh: 閣門使失儀，宣徽使糾之。

translations.literal: if the palace gate commissioner breached decorum, the Palace Domestic commissioner corrected him.
translations.idiomatic: if the gate commissioner erred, the Palace Domestic commissioner corrected him.

sentences.zh: 凡出者皆𣀃靴急趨揖殿。

translations.literal: All who went out stamped their boots, hurried, and bowed toward the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone leaving stamped his boots, hurried out, and bowed toward the hall.

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、學士就位，閣門使宣放仗，再拜，賜廊下食，又再拜。

translations.literal: next the Secretariat, Chancellery, and academicians took their places; the palace gate commissioner announced dismissal of the guard formation; they bowed twice, were granted food in the corridor below, and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Next Secretariat, Chancellery, and academicians took position; the gate commissioner announced dismissal of the guard; officials bowed twice, received corridor refreshments, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 次閣門使奏閣內無事，文武官出，殿上索扇，垂簾，輦還宮。

translations.literal: next the palace gate commissioner reported that there was no business within the palace hall; civil and military officials went out; on the hall fans were called for, curtains lowered, and the palanquin returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Next the gate commissioner reported no further business; civil and military officials withdrew; fans were called for, curtains lowered, and the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 其賜廊下食，自左右勤政門北東西兩廊，文東武西，以北為上立定；

translations.literal: As for the granted food in the corridor below, from north of the left and right Diligence-in-Government gates in the eastern and western corridors—civil east, military west—they stood fixed with north as superior;
translations.idiomatic: For corridor refreshments, officials stood in the eastern and western corridors north of the Diligence-in-Government gates—civil east, military west, higher rank to the north;

sentences.zh: 中丞至本位，麵南一揖，乃就坐食；

translations.literal: when the vice censor reached his place, he faced south, bowed once, then sat to eat;
translations.idiomatic: the vice censor reached his place, bowed once facing south, then sat to eat;

sentences.zh: 至台吏，讚乃搢笏食，食訖復讚，食畢而罷。

translations.literal: when it reached the censorate clerks, the announcer then intoned; they inserted their tablets and ate; when eating was finished the announcer intoned again, and when the meal was complete it ended.
translations.idiomatic: at the censorate clerks’ turn the announcer called; they tucked their tablets and ate; when finished the announcer called again, and the meal ended.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，命有司增黃麾仗三百五十人，令文武官隨中書、門下橫行起居，徙翰林學士位於參知政事後，與節度使分東西揖殿出。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, he ordered the responsible offices to add three hundred fifty men to the yellow-banner guard formation, ordered civil and military officials to follow the Secretariat and Chancellery in crosswise attendance, moved Hanlin academicians’ position behind the participation-in-governance councilors, and had them bow toward the hall and go out east and west with the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, he added 350 men to the yellow-banner guard, had civil and military officials follow Secretariat and Chancellery in crosswise attendance, placed Hanlin academicians after the vice grand councilors, and had them leave east and west with the military commissioners, bowing toward the hall.

sentences.zh: 真宗凡三行之，景德以後，其禮不行。

translations.literal: Zhenzong performed it three times in all; after Jingde the rite was no longer carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong held it three times; after Jingde the ceremony fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 仁宗從知制誥李淑議，仍讀時令，詔禮官詳定儀注，以言者謂未合典禮而罷。

translations.literal: Renzong followed the proposal of drafting edict officer Li Shu to continue reading the seasonal ordinances; he ordered ritual officials to fix the protocol in detail, but because critics said it did not accord with canonical ritual it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong accepted drafting edict officer Li Shu’s proposal to continue reading seasonal ordinances and ordered ritual officials to draft protocol, but critics said it violated canonical ritual and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，知制誥宋敏求等言：“奉詔重修定閣門儀制內文德殿殿入閣儀，按今文德殿，唐宣政殿也；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, drafting edict officer Song Minqiu and others said: “Receiving the edict to revise and fix the entering-the-palace-hall rite for the Hall of Civil Virtue within the palace gate regulations—according to investigation, the present Hall of Civil Virtue is the Tang Hall of Proclaiming Governance;
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3, drafting edict officer Song Minqiu and others said, “By edict we are revising the inner-hall protocol for the Hall of Civil Virtue in the palace gate regulations. The present Hall of Civil Virtue is the Tang Hall of Proclaiming Governance;

sentences.zh: 紫宸殿，唐紫宸殿也。

translations.literal: the Hall of Purple Eminence is the Tang Hall of Purple Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: the Hall of Purple Eminence is the Tang Hall of Purple Eminence.

sentences.zh: 然祖宗視朝，皆嘗御文德入閣。

translations.literal: Yet the founding emperors, when holding court, all once held the entering-the-palace-hall audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our founding emperors had all held inner-hall audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue.

sentences.zh: 唐制，常設仗衛於宣政殿，或遇上坐紫宸，即喚仗入閣。

translations.literal: Tang regulation constantly posted guard formations at the Hall of Proclaiming Governance; if on occasion the emperor sat in the Hall of Purple Eminence, he then summoned the guard formation to enter the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice guards were normally posted at the Hall of Proclaiming Governance; when the emperor sat in the Hall of Purple Eminence, he summoned them into the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 如此，則當御紫宸殿入閣，方合舊典。

translations.literal: In this way, he should hold the entering-the-palace-hall audience at the Hall of Purple Eminence to accord with the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: On that logic, inner-hall audience should be held at the Hall of Purple Eminence to match ancient practice.

sentences.zh: ”翰林學士王珪等議：“按入閣者，乃唐舊日紫宸殿受常朝之儀也。

translations.literal: ” Hanlin academician Wang Gui and others deliberated: “According to investigation, entering the palace hall was the Tang old rite for receiving regular audience at the Hall of Purple Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hanlin academician Wang Gui and others argued, “Entering the palace hall was originally the Tang routine for regular audience at the Hall of Purple Eminence.

sentences.zh: 唐紫宸與今同，宣政殿即今文德殿。

translations.literal: The Tang Hall of Purple Eminence is the same as the present one; the Hall of Proclaiming Governance is the present Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Hall of Purple Eminence is our present hall; the Hall of Proclaiming Governance is our Hall of Civil Virtue.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天子坐朝，必立仗於正衙。

translations.literal: Tang regulation: when the Son of Heaven sat in court, guard formations were always posted in the main audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, whenever the emperor held court, guards were posted in the main audience hall.

sentences.zh: 若止御紫宸，即喚正衙仗自宣政殿東西閣門入，故為入閣。

translations.literal: If he only held court in the Hall of Purple Eminence, he then summoned the main-hall guard formation to enter from the eastern and western palace-gate doors of the Hall of Proclaiming Governance—hence it was called entering the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: If he sat only in the Hall of Purple Eminence, he summoned the main-hall guard through the eastern and western gates of the Hall of Proclaiming Governance—hence “entering the palace hall.”

sentences.zh: 五代以來遂廢正衙立仗之制。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward the system of posting guards in the main audience hall was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties the main-hall guard posting had been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今閣門所載入閣儀者，止是唐常朝之儀，非盛禮也。

translations.literal: The entering-the-palace-hall rite now recorded in the palace gate regulations is only the Tang regular-audience rite, not a grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The inner-hall protocol in the gate regulations is only the Tang routine audience, not a major ceremony.

sentences.zh: ”自是入閣之禮遂罷。

translations.literal: ” From this the entering-the-palace-hall rite was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereafter the inner-hall ceremony was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 敏求又言：“本朝惟入閣乃御文德殿視朝，今既不用入閣儀，即文德遂闕視朝之禮。

translations.literal: Minqiu also said: “In this dynasty only entering the palace hall meant holding court at the Hall of Civil Virtue; now that the entering-the-palace-hall rite is no longer used, the Hall of Civil Virtue accordingly lacks the court-audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu added, “In our dynasty only the inner-hall ceremony brought audience to the Hall of Civil Virtue; now that it is discontinued, that hall has no audience ritual.

sentences.zh: 請下兩制及太常禮院，約唐制御宣政殿，裁定朔望御文德殿儀，以備正衙視朝之制。

translations.literal: We request that the two drafting offices and the Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered, approximating the Tang regulation for holding court at the Hall of Proclaiming Governance, to fix the rite for holding court at the Hall of Civil Virtue on the first and fifteenth of the month, to supply the main-audience-hall court system.”
translations.idiomatic: We ask the two drafting offices and the ritual directorate, following Tang practice at the Hall of Proclaiming Governance, to fix protocol for new- and full-moon audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue as a substitute for main-hall court.”

sentences.zh: ”學士韓維等以《入閣圖》增損裁定上儀曰：

translations.literal: ” Academicians Han Wei and others, using the “Diagram of Entering the Palace Hall” with additions and deletions, fixed and submitted the superior rite, saying:
translations.idiomatic: ” Academicians Han Wei and others revised the Diagram of Entering the Palace Hall and submitted revised protocol:

sentences.zh: 朔日不值假，前五日，閣門移諸司排辦，前一日，有司供帳文德殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the month, if it did not fall on a holiday, five days before the palace gate office notified the various offices to arrange matters; one day before, the responsible offices supplied the furnishings at the Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the month, if not a holiday, five days earlier the gate office notified all departments to prepare; the day before, officials set up the Hall of Civil Virtue.

sentences.zh: 其日，金吾將軍常服押本衛仗，判殿中省官押細仗，先入殿庭，東西對列；

translations.literal: On that day, the Golden Crow general in ordinary dress escorted his command’s guard formation; the acting director of the Palace Domestic Service escorted the detailed guard; they entered the palace courtyard first, arrayed facing each other east and west;
translations.idiomatic: That day the Golden Crow general in ordinary dress led his command’s guard, and the acting Palace Domestic director led the detailed guard; both entered the courtyard and faced off east and west;

sentences.zh: 文武官東西序立；

translations.literal: civil and military officials stood in order east and west;
translations.idiomatic: civil and military officials lined up east and west;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校分入，北向立；

translations.literal: various army officers entered separately and stood facing north;
translations.idiomatic: army officers entered in groups and stood facing north;

sentences.zh: 朝堂引讚官引彈奏御史二員入殿門踏道，當下殿北向立；

translations.literal: court lead-announcer officials led two impeachment censors through the palace gate onto the ramp, standing facing north below the hall;
translations.idiomatic: court announcers led two impeachment censors through the gate onto the ramp to stand below the hall, facing north;

sentences.zh: 次催文武班分入，並東西相向立；

translations.literal: next civil and military formations were urged in separately, all standing facing each other east and west;
translations.idiomatic: next civil and military ranks were ushered in to face each other east and west;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校即於殿庭北向立班。

translations.literal: the various army officers then lined up facing north in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: army officers then formed their north-facing line in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服靴袍御垂拱殿，鳴鞭，內侍、閣門、管軍依朔望常例起居；

translations.literal: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, held court at the Hall of Hanging Bow; whips were cracked; eunuchs, palace gate, and army controllers performed attendance according to the usual new- and full-moon practice;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in boots and robe, held court at the Hall of Hanging Bow; whips cracked; eunuchs, gate officers, and army controllers offered routine new- and full-moon attendance;

sentences.zh: 次引樞密、宣徽、三司使副、樞密直學士、內客省使以下至醫官、待詔及修起居注官二員並大起居。

translations.literal: next were led the privy council, Palace Domestic, three-commissioner deputies, privy council academicians, Inner Reception Bureau commissioner and below down to medical officers, awaiting-edict officials, and the two officials who compiled the attendance record, together with the great attendance.
translations.idiomatic: next came the privy council, Palace Domestic, fiscal commissioners’ deputies, privy council academicians, Inner Reception commissioner and subordinates down to medical officers and awaiting-edict officials, the two attendance recorders, and the grand attendance.

sentences.zh: 諸司使以下，退排立。

translations.literal: Various bureau commissioners and below withdrew and lined up in order.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners and below withdrew and formed ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝輦至文德殿後，閣門奏班齊，帝出，殿上索扇，升榻，鳴鞭；

translations.literal: When the emperor’s palanquin reached behind the Hall of Civil Virtue, the palace gate reported the formations complete; the emperor came out; on the hall fans were called for; he ascended the couch; whips were cracked;
translations.idiomatic: When the palanquin reached the rear of the Hall of Civil Virtue, the gate office reported ranks complete; the emperor emerged; fans were called for on the dais; he mounted the couch; whips cracked;

sentences.zh: 扇開，卷簾，儀鸞使焚香，喝文武官就位，四拜起居；

translations.literal: fans opened, curtains rolled up, the ceremonial guard commissioner burned incense, called civil and military officials to their places, four bows of attendance;
translations.idiomatic: fans opened, curtains rose, the ceremonial guard commissioner burned incense, called officials to position, and they bowed four times in attendance;

sentences.zh: 雞人唱時；

translations.literal: the cock-man announced the hour;
translations.idiomatic: the hour-announcer called the time;

sentences.zh: 舍人於彈奏御史班前西向喝大起居。

translations.literal: the palace secretary, west of the impeachment censor formation, called facing west for the great attendance.
translations.idiomatic: west of the impeachment censors, a palace secretary called for the grand attendance.

sentences.zh: 御史由文武班後至對立位，次引左右金吾將軍合班於宣制石南大起居，班首出班躬奏軍國內外平安，歸位再拜，各歸東西押仗位。

translations.literal: Censors passed behind the civil and military formations to the facing positions; next the left and right Golden Crow generals were led to combine formations south of the edict-proclaiming stone for the great attendance; the formation head left the line, bowed personally, and reported that within and without the army and state all was secure, returned to place and bowed twice, each returning to east and west escort-guard positions.
translations.idiomatic: Censors passed behind the civil and military ranks to facing positions; then left and right Golden Crow generals combined south of the edict stone for grand attendance; the lead officer stepped out, bowed, and reported peace throughout the realm, bowed twice, and each returned to his east or west escort post.

sentences.zh: 通喝舍人於宣制石南北向對立。

translations.literal: The general-announcing palace secretary stood facing each other north and south at the edict-proclaiming stone.
translations.idiomatic: General-announcing secretaries stood north and south of the edict stone, facing each other.

sentences.zh: 舍人退於西階，次揖宰臣、親王以下，躬奏文武百僚、宰臣某姓名以下起居，分引宰臣以下橫行，諸軍將校仍舊立。

translations.literal: The palace secretary withdrew to the western steps; next bowed to the chief councilor, imperial princes, and below; bowed personally and reported the attendance of the civil and military hundred officials, chief councilor so-and-so by name and below; separately led the chief councilor and below across; the various army officers still stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary withdrew to the western steps, then bowed to the chief councilor, princes, and others, reported attendance in the names of the hundred officials and chief councilor, and led the chief councilor’s party across while army officers held position.

sentences.zh: 閣門使喝大起居，舍人引宰臣至儀石北，俯伏跪致詞祝月訖，其詞云：“文武百僚、宰臣全銜臣某姓名等言：孟春之吉，伏惟皇帝陛下膺受時祉，與天無窮，臣等無任歡呼抃蹈之至。

translations.literal: The palace gate commissioner called for the great attendance; the palace secretary led the chief councilor north of the ritual stone; prostrate, kneeling, he finished the congratulatory words for the month; the words said: “The civil and military hundred officials, chief councilor with full title, your subject so-and-so by name and others say: On the auspicious day of mid-spring, we respectfully wish that Your Majesty the Emperor has received the timely blessing, without end together with Heaven—your subjects cannot bear the utmost of cheering and stamping joy.”
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner called grand attendance; the secretary led the chief councilor north of the ritual stone to kneel prostrate and offer the monthly congratulation: “The civil and military officials, Chief Councilor [full title] and your servant [name], on this auspicious day of mid-spring respectfully wish Your Majesty blessings without end as Heaven’s—your servants cannot contain our joy.”

sentences.zh: ”歸位五拜。

translations.literal: ” He returned to place and bowed five times.
translations.idiomatic: ” He returned to place and bowed five times.

sentences.zh: 閣門使揖中書由東階升殿，樞密使帶平章事以上由西階升殿侍立；

translations.literal: The palace gate commissioner bowed the Secretariat up the eastern steps to ascend the hall; the privy councilor with grand councilor and above ascended the western steps to attend standing;
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner ushered the Secretariat up the eastern steps; the privy councilor and grand councilors ascended the western steps to attend;

sentences.zh: 給事中一員歸左省位立；

translations.literal: one supervising secretary returned to the left-province position and stood;
translations.idiomatic: one supervising secretary took the left-province post;

sentences.zh: 轉對官立於給事中之南

translations.literal: the rotation-memorial official stood south of the supervising secretary
translations.idiomatic: the rotation-memorial official stood south of the supervising secretary

sentences.zh: （如罷轉對官，每遇御史台前期牒請。

translations.literal: (if the rotation-memorial official was abolished, whenever the Censorate beforehand sent a request slip.
translations.idiomatic: (if the rotation-memorial post was vacant, the Censorate submitted a request slip in advance.

sentences.zh: 文官二員並依轉對官例，先於閣門投進奏狀）〉

translations.literal: two civil officials both followed the rotation-memorial precedent, first submitting memorials at the palace gate))
translations.idiomatic: Two civil officials followed the same rule and filed memorials at the gate first)

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎及刑法官立於轉對官南；

translations.literal: the Personnel vice minister and penal-law officials stood south of the rotation-memorial official;
translations.idiomatic: the Personnel vice minister and penal-law officials stood south of the rotation-memorial official;

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎於右省班南，與吏部侍郎東西相向立，搢笏，各出班籍置笏上

translations.literal: the War vice minister south of the right-province formation, standing facing each other east and west with the Personnel vice minister, inserted their tablets, each left the formation and placed the roster and set the tablet on top
translations.idiomatic: the War vice minister south of the right-province line faced the Personnel vice minister east and west, tucked their tablets, stepped out, set the roster down, and placed their tablets on it

sentences.zh: （吏部、兵部侍郎以知審官東、西院官充，刑法官以知審刑、大理寺官充）〉

translations.literal: (the Personnel and War vice ministers were filled by officials who knew the eastern and western courts of the Personnel Evaluation Bureau; penal-law officials were filled by officials who knew the Penal Review and Court of Judicial Review))
translations.idiomatic: (Personnel and War vice ministers served ex officio as directors of the eastern and western evaluation courts; penal-law officials served as directors of penal review and the Court of Judicial Review)

sentences.zh: 親王、使相以下分班出；

translations.literal: imperial princes, commissioner-envoys, and below went out in separate formations;
translations.idiomatic: imperial princes, commissioner-envoys, and those below filed out by formation;

sentences.zh: 引轉對官於宣制石南，宣徽使殿上承旨宣答如儀；

translations.literal: the rotation-memorial official was led south of the edict-proclaiming stone; the Palace Domestic commissioner on the hall received the edict and proclaimed the reply according to the rite;
translations.idiomatic: the rotation-memorial official was led south of the edict stone; the Palace Domestic commissioner on the dais received and proclaimed the imperial reply as prescribed;

sentences.zh: 次吏部、兵部侍郎及刑法官對揖出；

translations.literal: next the Personnel and War vice ministers and penal-law officials bowed to each other in pairs and went out;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Personnel and War vice ministers and penal-law officials exchanged paired bows and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次彈奏御史無彈奏對揖出

translations.literal: next the impeachment censor, if there was no impeachment, bowed in pairs and went out
translations.idiomatic: Next the impeachment censor, if there was no impeachment to report, exchanged paired bows and withdrew

sentences.zh: （如有彈奏，並如儀）〉

translations.literal: (if there was impeachment, all followed the rite))
translations.idiomatic: (if there was impeachment, protocol was followed as usual)

sentences.zh: 引給事中至宣制石南揖，躬奏殿中無事；

translations.literal: the supervising secretary was led to south of the edict-proclaiming stone and bowed; bowing personally, he reported that there was no business in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary was led south of the edict stone to bow and report personally that there was no further business in the hall;

sentences.zh: 喝祗候，揖，西出；

translations.literal: called to attend; bowed; went out to the west;
translations.idiomatic: was called to attend, bowed, and exited to the west;

sentences.zh: 次引修起居注官，次引排立供奉官以下各合班於宣制石南躬；

translations.literal: next were led the officials who compiled the attendance record; next were led the lined-up attendant officials and below, each combining formations south of the edict-proclaiming stone and bowing personally;
translations.idiomatic: next came the attendance recorders, then attendant officials and below, who combined formations south of the edict stone and bowed;

sentences.zh: 喝祗候揖，分班出；

translations.literal: called to attend and bow; went out in separate formations;
translations.idiomatic: were called to attend and bow, then filed out by formation;

sentences.zh: 喝天武官等門外祗候，出。

translations.literal: called the Celestial Martial officers and others to attend outside the gate; went out.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Martial officers and others were called to wait outside the gate, then all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 索扇，垂簾，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭；

translations.literal: Fans were called for; curtains lowered; the emperor descended from the seat; whips were cracked;
translations.idiomatic: Fans were called for, curtains lowered, the emperor left the seat, and whips cracked;

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿承旨放仗，四色官𣀃靴急趨至宣制石南，稱奉敕放仗。

translations.literal: The palace secretary, receiving the edict at the hall, dismissed the guard formation; the four-color officers stamped their boots and hurried to south of the edict-proclaiming stone, proclaiming that by imperial command the guard formation was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary, on imperial order at the dais, dismissed the guard; four-color officers stamped their boots, hurried south of the edict stone, and announced dismissal of the guard by imperial command.

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍並判殿中省官對拜，訖，隨仗出，親王、使相、節度使至刺史、學士、台省官、諸軍將校等並序班朝堂，謝賜茶酒。

translations.literal: The Golden Crow general and the acting director of the Palace Domestic Service bowed to each other; when finished, they followed the guard formation out; imperial princes, commissioner-envoys, military commissioners down to prefects, academicians, capital and provincial officials, various army officers and others all lined up in order in the court hall and thanked the emperor for the granted tea and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Crow general and acting Palace Domestic director exchanged bows, then followed the guard out; princes, commissioner-envoys, military commissioners down to prefects, academicians, capital officials, and army officers lined up in the court hall to thank the emperor for tea and wine.

sentences.zh: 帝復御垂拱殿，中書、樞密及請對官奏事；

translations.literal: The emperor again held court at the Hall of Hanging Bow; the Secretariat, privy council, and officials requesting audience reported business;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the Hall of Hanging Bow, where the Secretariat, privy council, and petitioners presented business;

sentences.zh: 不引見謝、辭班。

translations.literal: The formations for audience-thanks and leave-taking were not led in.
translations.idiomatic: Formations for thanks and farewell audiences were not introduced.

sentences.zh: 後殿坐，臨時取旨。

translations.literal: He sat in the rear hall and took edicts on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the rear hall he took audience and issued orders as needed.

sentences.zh: 其日遇有德音、制書、御劄，仍候退御垂拱殿坐，制箱出外。

translations.literal: If on that day there were gracious edicts, proclamation documents, or imperial letters, they still waited until he withdrew to sit in the Hall of Hanging Bow, and the document box was taken outside.
translations.idiomatic: If gracious edicts, proclamations, or imperial letters were issued that day, they waited until the emperor withdrew to the Hall of Hanging Bow, then brought the document box out.

sentences.zh: 應正衙見、謝、辭文武臣僚，並依御史台儀制喚班，依序分入於文武班後，以北為首，分東西相向，重行異位，依見、辭、謝班序位。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials who should have main-audience-hall audience, thanks, or leave-taking all had their formations called according to Censorate regulations; in order they entered separately behind the civil and military formations, with north as head, split east and west facing each other, double rows in separate positions, according to the sequence of audience, leave-taking, and thanks formations.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials due for main-hall audience, thanks, or farewell were called to formation per Censorate regulations, entered in order behind the civil and military ranks with seniority to the north, faced off east and west in double rows, and took positions according to audience protocol.

sentences.zh: 餘押班臣僚於班稍前押班，候刑法官對揖出，分引近前揖躬。

translations.literal: The remaining formation-escort officials escorted the formation slightly forward; when penal-law officials bowed in pairs and went out, they were separately led forward to bow personally.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining escort officials moved their formations slightly forward; when penal-law officials withdrew with paired bows, they were led forward separately to bow in person.

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿宣班，引轉對班見、謝、辭，並如紫宸儀。

translations.literal: The palace secretary at the hall announced the formation; led the rotation-memorial formation for audience, thanks, and leave-taking—all as in the Hall of Purple Eminence rite.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary announced formations at the dais and led rotation-memorial audiences for presentation, thanks, and farewell, all per Hall of Purple Eminence protocol.

sentences.zh: 樞密使不帶平章事、參知政事至同簽書樞密院事、宣徽使並立於宣制石南稍北，宰臣、親王、樞密使帶平章事、使相係押班者，立於儀石南，餘官並立於宣制石南，如合通喚，閣門使引並如儀。

translations.literal: The privy councilor without grand councilor title, participation-in-governance councilor down to co-signatory of the Privy Council, and Palace Domestic commissioner all stood slightly north of south of the edict-proclaiming stone; the chief councilor, imperial princes, privy councilor with grand councilor title, and commissioner-envoys who were formation escorts stood south of the ritual stone; all other officials stood south of the edict-proclaiming stone; if they should be summoned together, the palace gate commissioner led them—all according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Privy councilors without grand councilor rank, vice grand councilors, co-signatories, and the Palace Domestic commissioner stood just north of the edict stone; chief councilors, princes, privy councilors with grand councilor rank, and escorting commissioner-envoys stood south of the ritual stone; other officials stood south of the edict stone; when summoned together, the gate commissioner led them per protocol.

sentences.zh: 讚喝訖，係中書、樞密並揖升殿辭謝，揖，西出，其合問聖體者，並如儀；

translations.literal: When the announcer had finished calling, those attached to the Secretariat and privy council together bowed, ascended the hall, took leave and thanked, bowed, and went out to the west; those who should inquire after the Sacred Person—all according to the rite;
translations.idiomatic: When announcements ended, Secretariat and privy council officials bowed, ascended to take leave and offer thanks, bowed again, and exited west; those who should inquire after the emperor’s health did so per protocol;

sentences.zh: 餘官分班出

translations.literal: the remaining officials went out in separate formations
translations.idiomatic: remaining officials filed out by formation

sentences.zh: （彈奏御史候見、謝、辭班絕，對揖出。

translations.literal: (the impeachment censor waited until the audience, thanks, and leave-taking formations were finished, then bowed in pairs and went out.
translations.idiomatic: (the impeachment censor waited until audience, thanks, and farewell formations ended, then exchanged paired bows and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其朝見，如謝都城門外御筵，及召赴闕謝茶藥撫問之類，不可合班者，各依別班中謝對。

translations.literal: For court audiences such as thanking for the imperial banquet outside the capital gate, or being summoned to court to thank for tea, medicine, and imperial inquiries—cases that could not combine formations—each followed a separate formation to offer thanks and reply in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Audiences such as thanks for the imperial banquet outside the capital gate, or summons to court to thank for tea, medicine, or imperial inquiries—cases that could not share a formation—each used a separate formation for thanks and reply.

sentences.zh: 賜酒食等並門賜。

translations.literal: Granted wine, food, and the like were all granted at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wine, food, and similar gifts were all bestowed at the gate.

sentences.zh: 其係正衙見門謝辭，亦門外唱放）〉

translations.literal: Those attached to main-audience-hall audience who thanked and took leave at the gate also had dismissal announced outside the gate))
translations.idiomatic: Those with main-hall audience who thanked and took leave at the gate also had dismissal announced outside the gate)

sentences.zh: 應正衙見、謝、辭臣僚，前一日於閣門投詣正衙榜子，閣門上奏目；

translations.literal: Officials who should have main-audience-hall audience, thanks, or leave-taking, on the day before submitted at the palace gate the placard requesting main-audience-hall audience; the palace gate reported the list upward;
translations.idiomatic: Officials due for main-hall audience, thanks, or farewell submitted a request placard at the gate the day before, and the gate office reported the list upward;

sentences.zh: 又投正衙狀於御史台、四方館。

translations.literal: They also submitted main-audience-hall memorials to the Censorate and the Four Directions Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: They also filed main-hall memorials with the Censorate and the Four Directions Hostel.

sentences.zh: 應朔日或得旨罷文德殿視朝，止御紫宸殿起居，其已上奏目。

translations.literal: If on the first of the month or by received edict audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue was canceled, holding court only at the Hall of Purple Eminence for attendance—the list already reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: If the first of the month or an edict canceled audience at the Hall of Civil Virtue and court was held only at the Hall of Purple Eminence, the list already submitted still applied.

sentences.zh: 正衙見、謝、辭班並放免，依官品隨赴紫宸殿引，或值改，依常朝文德殿，自有百官班日，並如舊儀。

translations.literal: Main-audience-hall audience, thanks, and leave-taking formations were all exempted; according to official rank they followed to be led at the Hall of Purple Eminence; if the date changed, they followed regular court at the Hall of Civil Virtue; on days when all officials had formations, all followed the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: Main-hall audience, thanks, and farewell formations were waived; by rank officials were led to the Hall of Purple Eminence; if the schedule changed, regular court at the Hall of Civil Virtue applied; on days when all officials had formations, old protocol was followed.

sentences.zh: 應外國蕃客見、辭，候喚班先引赴殿庭東，依本國職次重行異位立，候見、辭、謝班絕，西向躬。

translations.literal: For foreign tributary guests having audience or leave-taking, when their formation was called they were first led to the east of the palace courtyard; according to their state’s ranks they stood in double rows in separate positions; when audience, leave-taking, and thanks formations were finished, they bowed facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign tributary guests due for audience or farewell were led to the east courtyard when called, stood in double rows by their state’s ranks, and bowed west when audience formations ended.

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿通班轉於宣制石南，北向立，讚喝如儀，西出。

translations.literal: The palace secretary at the hall announced the formation’s passage, turned south of the edict-proclaiming stone, stood facing north, called according to the rite, and went out to the west.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary announced the formation, moved south of the edict stone, stood facing north, called per protocol, and exited west.

sentences.zh: 其酒食分物並門賜，如有進奉，候彈奏御史出，進奉入

translations.literal: Their wine, food, and distributed items were all granted at the gate; if there were tribute offerings, they waited until the impeachment censor went out, then tribute entered
translations.idiomatic: Wine, food, and distributed gifts were granted at the gate; if tribute was presented, it entered after the impeachment censor withdrew

sentences.zh: （唯御馬及擔床自殿西偏門入，東偏門出。

translations.literal: (only imperial horses and carrying couches entered through the western side gate of the hall and exited through the eastern side gate.
translations.idiomatic: (only imperial horses and carrying couches entered through the hall’s western side gate and exited through the eastern side gate.

sentences.zh: 其進奉出入，文武官起居，舍人通某國進奉，宣徽使喝進奉出，節次如紫宸儀）〉

translations.literal: As tribute went in and out, civil and military officials performed attendance; the palace secretary announced such-and-such state’s tribute; the Palace Domestic commissioner called tribute out; the sequence as in the Hall of Purple Eminence rite))
translations.idiomatic: As tribute entered and left, civil and military officials offered attendance, the secretary announced each state’s tribute, the Palace Domestic commissioner called tribute out, in the same order as Hall of Purple Eminence protocol)

sentences.zh: 候進奉出，給事中奏殿中無事，出。

translations.literal: When tribute had gone out, the supervising secretary reported that there was no business in the hall, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: After tribute withdrew, the supervising secretary reported no further business and left.

sentences.zh: 其後殿再坐，合引出者，從別儀。

translations.literal: If he sat again in the rear hall, those who should be led out followed separate protocol.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor sat again in the rear hall, those to be introduced followed separate protocol.

sentences.zh: 其日，賜茶酒，宰臣、樞密於閣子，親王於本廳，使相、宣徽使、兩省官、待制、三司副使、文武百官、皇親使相以下至率府副率，及四廂都指揮使以下至副都頭，並於朝堂

translations.literal: On that day, when tea and wine were granted: chief councilors and privy council at the side chamber; imperial princes at their own hall; commissioner-envoys, Palace Domestic commissioner, two-province officials, awaiting-edict officials, fiscal commission deputies, civil and military hundred officials, imperial clansmen and commissioner-envoys down to deputy commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, and four-corridor supreme commanders down to deputy company heads—all at the court hall
translations.idiomatic: That day, tea and wine were granted at the court hall to chief councilors and the privy council in the side chamber, princes in their own halls, and commissioner-envoys, Palace Domestic commissioner, two-province officials, awaiting-edict officials, fiscal deputies, civil and military officials, imperial clansmen down to deputy commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, and four-corridor commanders down to deputy company heads

sentences.zh: （如朝堂位次不足，即於朝堂門外設次）〉

translations.literal: (if positions in the court hall were insufficient, then set up stations outside the court hall gate))
translations.idiomatic: (if the court hall could not hold all ranks, stations were set up outside the gate)

sentences.zh: 管軍節度使至四廂都指揮使、節度使、兩使留後至刺史，並於客省廳。

translations.literal: Army-controlling military commissioners down to four-corridor supreme commanders, military commissioners, two-commissioner military governors and regents down to prefects—all at the Guest Reception Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Army-controlling military commissioners, four-corridor supreme commanders, military commissioners, regents, and prefects all received refreshments in the Guest Reception Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔從所定。

translations.literal: An edict followed what had been fixed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted these provisions.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初建明堂，禮制局列上七議：

translations.literal: When Huizong first built the Hall of Brightness, the Ritual Regulations Bureau submitted seven proposals:
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong first built the Hall of Brightness, the Ritual Regulations Bureau submitted seven proposals:

sentences.zh: 一曰：古者朔必告廟，示不敢專。

translations.literal: First: In antiquity on the first of the month one always reported to the ancestral temple, showing that one did not dare act alone.
translations.idiomatic: First: In antiquity the new moon was always reported at the ancestral temple, showing that the ruler did not act alone.

sentences.zh: 請視朝聽朔必先奏告，以見繼述之意。

translations.literal: We request that holding court and receiving the new moon must first be reported in memorial, to show the intent of continuing the succession.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that court audience on the new moon be preceded by a memorial report to the temple, expressing continuity with past rulers.

sentences.zh: 二曰：古者天子負扆南向以朝諸侯，聽朔則各隨其方。

translations.literal: Second: In antiquity the Son of Heaven, leaning on the screen and facing south, received the feudal lords; when receiving the new moon each followed his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Second: In antiquity the emperor, leaning on the screen facing south, received the feudal lords; at the new moon audience each stood according to his direction.

sentences.zh: 請自今御明堂正南向之位，布政則隨月而御堂，其閏月則居門焉。

translations.literal: We request that from now he hold the due-south position at the Hall of Brightness; when promulgating government he should hold court in the hall according to the month; in intercalary months he should occupy the gate position.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter he take the due-south seat at the Hall of Brightness, hold the monthly hall according to the month when promulgating policy, and occupy the gate position in intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 三曰：《禮記•月令》，天子居青陽、總章，每月異禮。

translations.literal: Third: In “Monthly Ordinances” in the Book of Rites, the Son of Heaven dwelt in Green Yang and Total Splendor; each month had different rites.
translations.idiomatic: Third: The Book of Rites’ “Monthly Ordinances” has the Son of Heaven dwell in Green Yang and Total Splendor, with different rites each month.

sentences.zh: 請稽《月令》十二堂之制，修定時令，使有司奉而行之。

translations.literal: We request investigation of the twelve-hall system in “Monthly Ordinances,” revision and fixing of seasonal ordinances, and that the responsible offices receive and carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the twelve-hall system in the Monthly Ordinances be studied, seasonal ordinances revised, and responsible offices ordered to enforce them.

sentences.zh: 四曰：《月令》以季秋之月為來歲受朔之日。

translations.literal: Fourth: “Monthly Ordinances” takes the month of late autumn as the day for receiving the new moon of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: The Monthly Ordinances designate late autumn as the day to receive the coming year’s new moon.

sentences.zh: 請以每歲十月於明堂受新曆，退而頒之郡國。

translations.literal: We request that every year in the tenth month at the Hall of Brightness he receive the new calendar, withdraw, and promulgate it to commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that each year in the tenth month at the Hall of Brightness he receive the new calendar and then promulgate it to the commanderies and states.

sentences.zh: 五曰：古者天子負扆，公、侯、伯、子、男、蠻夷戎狄四塞之國各以內外尊卑為位。

translations.literal: Fifth: In antiquity the Son of Heaven leaned on the screen; dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and the states of the four barriers of the barbarians, Yi, Rong, and Di each took position according to inner and outer precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: In antiquity the emperor leaned on the screen while dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and frontier states of the four quarters took position by rank, inner and outer.

sentences.zh: 請自今元正、冬至及大朝會並御明堂，遼使依賓禮，蕃國各隨其方，立於四門之外。

translations.literal: We request that from now on New Year’s Day, winter solstice, and great court assemblies all be held at the Hall of Brightness; Liao envoys follow guest rites; tributary states each follow their direction and stand outside the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that New Year’s Day, the winter solstice, and major court assemblies hereafter be held at the Hall of Brightness, with Liao envoys under guest rites and tributary states standing outside the four gates by direction.

sentences.zh: 六曰：古者以明堂為布政之宮，自今若有御劄、手詔並請先於明堂宣示，然後榜之朝堂，頒之天下。

translations.literal: Sixth: In antiquity the Hall of Brightness was the palace for promulgating government; from now if there are imperial letters or handwritten edicts, we request that they first be proclaimed at the Hall of Brightness, then posted in the court hall and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: In antiquity the Hall of Brightness was the seat of government; we ask that imperial letters and handwritten edicts hereafter be proclaimed there first, then posted in the court hall and issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 七曰：赦書、德音，舊制宣於文德殿，自今非御樓肆赦，並於明堂宣讀。

translations.literal: Seventh: Amnesty documents and gracious edicts, by old regulation were proclaimed at the Hall of Civil Virtue; from now, unless granting amnesty from the tower, all shall be read at the Hall of Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: Amnesty documents and gracious edicts were formerly proclaimed at the Hall of Civil Virtue; we ask that hereafter, except when granting amnesty from the tower, all be read at the Hall of Brightness.

sentences.zh: 政和七年九月一日，詔頒朔、布政自十月為始。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month of the seventh year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered that promulgating the new moon and government begin from the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month of Zhenghe 7, an edict ordered that promulgation of the new moon and government begin in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 是月一日，上御明堂平朔左個，頒天運、政治及八年戊戍歲運、曆數於天下。

translations.literal: On the first day of that month, the emperor held court at the Hall of Brightness, Level New Moon, left bay, and promulgated celestial cycles, government, and the eighth-year wuxu year-cycle, calendrical numbers to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of that month the emperor took the left bay of the Level New Moon hall at the Hall of Brightness and promulgated celestial cycles, government policy, and the wuxu eighth-year calendrical data throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是每月朔御明堂布是月之政。

translations.literal: From this, on each month’s first day he held court at the Hall of Brightness and promulgated that month’s government.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter on each new moon he held court at the Hall of Brightness to promulgate that month’s policy.

sentences.zh: 先是，群臣五上表請負扆聽朝，詔弗允，至是復再請，始從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the hundred officials five times submitted memorials requesting that he lean on the screen and hold court; an edict did not grant it; at this time they again requested twice, and he first consented.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the officials had five times memorialized asking him to lean on the screen and hold court; the throne had refused; now they asked again and he consented.

sentences.zh: 十一月一日上御明堂，南面以朝百辟，退坐於平朔頒政。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month the emperor held court at the Hall of Brightness, facing south to receive the hundred officials; he withdrew and sat at Level New Moon to promulgate government.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month he held court at the Hall of Brightness facing south to receive the officials, then withdrew to Level New Moon to promulgate policy.

sentences.zh: 其禮：百官常服立明堂下，乘輿自內殿出，負坐斧扆明堂。

translations.literal: The rite: the hundred officials in ordinary dress stood below the Hall of Brightness; the imperial carriage came out from the inner hall; leaning, he sat on the axe-screen at the Hall of Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual: officials in ordinary dress stood below the hall; the imperial carriage emerged from the inner palace; leaning on the axe-screen, he sat in the Hall of Brightness.

sentences.zh: 大晟樂作，百官朝於堂下，大臣升階進呈所頒布時令，左右丞一員跪請付外施行，宰相承制可之，左右丞乃下授頒政官，頒政官受而讀之訖，出，閣門奏禮畢。

translations.literal: Great Splendor music played; the hundred officials attended below the hall; great ministers ascended the steps and presented the seasonal ordinances to be promulgated; one left and right vice director kneeled and requested transmission outside for implementation; the chief councilor received the command and approved; the left and right vice directors then descended and handed them to the government-promulgation officer; the government-promulgation officer received and finished reading them, went out; the palace gate reported the rite complete.
translations.idiomatic: Great Splendor music played as officials attended below; senior ministers ascended to present the seasonal ordinances; one vice director knelt to request transmission for implementation; the chief councilor approved; the vice directors handed the text to the promulgation officer, who read it aloud; the gate office then reported the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 帝降坐，百官乃退。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the seat; the hundred officials then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left his seat and the officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是以為常。

translations.literal: From this it became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: This became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 其歲運、曆數、天運、政治之辭，文多不載。

translations.literal: The wording of the year-cycle, calendrical numbers, celestial cycles, and government policy is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The texts of the year-cycle, calendrical data, celestial cycles, and policy are mostly not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 是後則各隨歲月星曆氣運推移沿改，而易其辭焉。

translations.literal: After this each followed the shifting years, months, stars, calendars, and qi cycles along alterations, and the wording was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the wording changed each year with the calendrical and celestial cycles.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書左丞薛昂條具崇寧以來紹述熙、豐政事，各條其節目，係之月令，頒於明堂。

translations.literal: Initially, Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Xue Ang itemized the continuing of Xi and Feng government affairs since Chongning, each itemizing its entries, attaching them to the monthly ordinances, and promulgating them at the Hall of Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Left Vice Minister Xue Ang itemized policies continuing the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms since Chongning, arranged them under the monthly ordinances, and promulgated them at the Hall of Brightness.

sentences.zh: 尋詔：“頒月之朔，使民知寒暑燥濕之化，而萬里之遠，雖驛置日行五百里，已不及時。

translations.literal: Soon an edict said: “Promulgating the month’s new moon lets the people know the transformations of cold, heat, dryness, and wetness—but ten thousand li distant, even with relay posts traveling five hundred li a day, it is already not in time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict said, “Promulgating policy at the new moon lets the people know seasonal change—but even relay posts traveling five hundred li a day cannot reach ten thousand li in time.

sentences.zh: 其千里外當前期十日進呈取旨，頒布諸州長吏封掌，俟月朔宣讀之。

translations.literal: Beyond a thousand li, ten days before the period they should present upward to receive the edict; promulgate to the chief officials of the prefectures to seal and keep; wait until the month’s first day to proclaim and read it.”
translations.idiomatic: Beyond a thousand li, the text should be submitted ten days in advance for approval, sealed by prefectural chiefs, and read aloud on the new moon.”

translations.literal: ” (close of edict quotation).
translations.idiomatic: ” (end of edict).

sentences.zh: 御樓肆赦。

translations.literal: Granting amnesty from the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Granting Amnesty from the Tower

sentences.zh: 每郊祀前一日，有司設百官、親王、蕃國諸州朝貢使、僧道、耆老位宣德門外，太常設宮縣、鉦鼓。

translations.literal: On the day before each suburban sacrifice, the responsible offices set positions outside the Xuande Gate for the hundred officials, imperial princes, tributary envoys from the states, monks and Daoists, and elders; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set palace bells and gongs and drums.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before each suburban sacrifice, officials set places outside the Xuande Gate for officials, princes, tributary envoys, monks, Daoists, and elders; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set palace bells, gongs, and drums.

sentences.zh: 其日，刑部錄諸囚以俟。

translations.literal: On that day, the Ministry of Justice recorded all prisoners to await.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Ministry of Justice recorded all prisoners awaiting release.

sentences.zh: 駕還至宣德門內幄次，改常服，群臣就位，帝登樓御坐，樞密使、宣徽使侍立，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the inner screen tent at the Xuande Gate, he changed to ordinary dress; the hundred officials took position; the emperor ascended the tower and took the imperial seat; the privy councilor and Palace Domestic commissioner attended standing; guard formations as in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned to the tent inside the Xuande Gate, the emperor changed to ordinary dress; officials took position; he ascended the tower; the privy councilor and Palace Domestic commissioner stood in attendance; guards formed per protocol.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引群臣橫行再拜訖，復位。

translations.literal: The general-affairs palace secretary led the hundred officials to bow twice crosswise; when finished, they returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The general-affairs secretary led officials in a crosswise double bow, then they returned to position.

sentences.zh: 侍臣宣曰“承旨”，舍人詣樓前，侍臣宣敕立金雞。

translations.literal: An attending minister proclaimed “Receive the edict”; the palace secretary went before the tower; the attending minister proclaimed the edict to set up the golden rooster.
translations.idiomatic: An attending minister announced “Receive the edict”; the secretary went before the tower; the minister proclaimed the edict to erect the golden rooster.

sentences.zh: 舍人退詣班南，宣付所司訖，太常擊鼓集囚。

translations.literal: The palace secretary withdrew to south of the formation, proclaimed and handed over to the responsible office; when finished, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices struck drums to assemble prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary withdrew south of the formation, announced transfer to the responsible office, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices drummed to assemble the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 少府監立雞竿於樓東南隅，竿末伎人四面緣繩爭上，取雞口所銜絳幡，獲者即與之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of the Palace Workshops set up the rooster pole at the tower’s southeast corner; at the pole’s end performers on four sides climbed the rope competing upward, took the crimson banner held in the rooster’s mouth—whoever obtained it was given it.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Workshops directorate erected the rooster pole at the tower’s southeast corner; performers climbed the ropes from four sides to seize the crimson banner in the rooster’s beak, and whoever reached it received it.

sentences.zh: 樓上以朱絲繩貫木鶴，仙人乘之，奉制書循繩而下，至地，以畫台承鶴，有司取制書置案上。

translations.literal: On the tower a red silk rope threaded a wooden crane; an immortal rode it, bearing the proclamation document down the rope to the ground; a painted platform received the crane; the responsible office took the proclamation document and placed it on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: On the tower a red silk rope lowered a wooden crane ridden by an immortal bearing the proclamation; at ground level a painted platform received it; officials placed the document on the desk.

sentences.zh: 閣門使承旨引案宣付中書、門下，轉授通事舍人，北面宣云“有制”，百官再拜。

translations.literal: The palace gate commissioner, receiving the edict, led the desk and proclaimed, handing over to the Secretariat and Chancellery; it was transferred to the general-affairs palace secretary, who facing north proclaimed “There is a proclamation”; the hundred officials bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner, on imperial order, led the desk and handed the document to the Secretariat and Chancellery, then to the general-affairs secretary, who facing north announced “There is a proclamation”; officials bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣赦訖，還授中書、門下，付刑部侍郎承旨放囚，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: When the amnesty proclamation was finished, it was returned to the Secretariat and Chancellery and handed to the vice minister of Justice, who received the edict and released prisoners; the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty was proclaimed, the document returned to the Secretariat and Chancellery and was handed to the vice minister of Justice to release prisoners; officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 閣門使進詣前，承旨宣答訖，百官又再拜、舞蹈，退。

translations.literal: The palace gate commissioner advanced before him; receiving the edict, he proclaimed the reply; when finished, the hundred officials again bowed twice and performed the dance, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner advanced, proclaimed the imperial reply, and officials bowed twice, performed the dance of homage, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 若德音、赦書自內出者，並如文德殿宣制之儀。

translations.literal: If gracious edicts or amnesty documents came from within, all followed the rite for proclaiming documents at the Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gracious edicts or amnesty documents issued from within followed the Hall of Civil Virtue proclamation protocol.

sentences.zh: 其降御劄，亦閣門使跪授殿門外置箱中，百官班定，閣門授宰臣讀訖，傳告，百僚皆拜舞稱萬歲。

translations.literal: As for issued imperial letters, the palace gate commissioner also knelt and handed them outside the hall gate to be placed in a box; when the hundred officials’ formation was set, the palace gate handed them to the chief councilor to finish reading, announced transmission, and the hundred officials all bowed, danced, and proclaimed “Ten thousand years.”
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters were kneel-presented by the gate commissioner outside the hall gate and placed in a box; when officials were in formation, the gate commissioner gave them to the chief councilor to read aloud; on announcement all officials bowed, danced, and shouted “Ten thousand years.”

sentences.zh: 真宗宣制，有司請用儀仗四千人，自承天殿設細仗導衛，近臣起居訖，則分左右前導之。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong proclaimed a document, the responsible offices requested use of a guard formation of four thousand men; from the Hall of Receiving Heaven they set out the detailed guard as escort; when close ministers had finished attendance, they then split left and right to lead the way before.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong proclaimed a document, officials requested a guard of four thousand men; from the Hall of Receiving Heaven a detailed guard escorted him; after close ministers had attended, they split left and right to lead the way.

sentences.zh: 皇太后臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held court and governed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager Holds Court and Governs

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，真宗崩，遺旨以皇帝尚幼，軍國事兼權取皇太后處分。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, Zhenzong died; the testamentary instruction said that because the emperor was still young, military and state affairs were jointly to be provisionally taken and disposed of by the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianxing 1, Zhenzong died; his testament directed that because the emperor was still young, military and state affairs were provisionally to be handled by the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 宰相率百官稱賀，復前奉慰，又慰皇太后於簾前。

translations.literal: The chief councilor led the hundred officials in offering congratulations, again advanced to offer condolences, and again offered condolences to the empress dowager before the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor led officials in congratulations, then advanced to offer condolences and to console the empress dowager before the curtain.

sentences.zh: 有司詳定儀式：內東門拜表，合差入內都知一員跪授傳進；

translations.literal: The responsible offices fixed the protocol in detail: memorials bowed at the inner eastern gate should have one inner-palace director assigned to kneel, receive, and transmit inward;
translations.idiomatic: Officials fixed the protocol in detail: memorials presented at the inner eastern gate required one inner-palace director to kneel, receive, and transmit them inward;

sentences.zh: 皇太后所降批答，首書“覽表具之”，末云“所請宜許”或“不許”。

translations.literal: In the empress dowager’s issued written replies, the beginning wrote “I have read the memorial and noted it,” and the end said “what is requested should be granted” or “not granted.”
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager’s written replies began with “I have read the memorial and noted it” and ended with “the request is granted” or “not granted.”

sentences.zh: 初，丁謂定皇太后稱 “予”，中書與禮院參議，每下制令稱“予”，便殿處分稱“吾”。

translations.literal: Initially, Ding Wei fixed that the empress dowager should call herself “I”; the Secretariat and ritual directorate deliberated together; each time she issued a regulation she called herself “I,” and for side-hall dispositions she called herself “we.”
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ding Wei prescribed that the empress dowager use “I” in formal edicts and “we” in informal orders from the side hall, after deliberation with the Secretariat and ritual directorate.

sentences.zh: 皇太后詔：“止稱‘吾’，與皇帝並御承明殿垂簾決事。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued an edict: “Use only ‘we,’ and together with the emperor hold court behind the curtain at the Hall of Receiving Brightness to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager decreed, “Use only ‘we,’ and together with the emperor hold court behind the curtain at the Hall of Receiving Brightness to decide affairs.

sentences.zh: ”百官表賀。

translations.literal: ” The hundred officials submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: ” Officials submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，輔臣請與皇太后權同聽政。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne, assisting ministers requested that together with the empress dowager they provisionally share in hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, his ministers asked that he and the empress dowager provisionally govern together.

sentences.zh: 禮院議：自四月內東門小殿垂簾，兩府合班起居，以次奏事，非時召學士亦許至小殿。

translations.literal: The ritual directorate deliberated: from the fourth month, behind the curtain at the small hall inside the inner eastern gate; the two councils combined formations for attendance; in order they reported business; if summoned out of season, academicians were also permitted to come to the small hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual directorate decided that from the fourth month the empress dowager would hold court behind the curtain in the small hall at the inner eastern gate; the two councils would attend in combined formation and report business in turn; academicians summoned out of season might also enter the small hall.

sentences.zh: 時帝以疾權居柔儀殿東閣西室，太后垂簾處分稱“吾”，唯兩府日入候問聖體，因奏政事，退詣小殿簾外，覆奏太后。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor because of illness provisionally dwelt in the western chamber of the eastern pavilion of the Hall of Gentle Rites; the empress dowager behind the curtain disposed of affairs calling herself “we”; only the two councils daily entered to inquire after the Sacred Person, and thereby reported government affairs; withdrawing, they went before the small hall outside the curtain and reported again to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, ill, stayed provisionally in the western chamber of the eastern pavilion of the Hall of Gentle Rites; the empress dowager governed behind the curtain as “we”; only the two councils entered daily to inquire after his health and report affairs, then withdrew to report again outside the curtain of the small hall.

sentences.zh: 帝疾間，御前後殿聽政，兩府退朝，猶於小殿覆奏。

translations.literal: When the emperor’s illness eased, he held court in the front and rear halls; when the two councils withdrew from court, they still reported again at the small hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered somewhat, he held court in the front and rear halls; after the two councils withdrew, they still reported to the empress dowager at the small hall.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，太皇太后權同聽政。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, the grand empress dowager provisionally shared in hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, the grand empress dowager provisionally shared in government.

sentences.zh: 三省、樞密院按儀注：未釋服以前，遇隻日皇帝御迎陽門，日參官並赴起居，依例奏事。

translations.literal: The three provinces and Privy Council followed the protocol: before mourning garments were removed, on odd-numbered days the emperor held court at the Welcome-the-Sun Gate; daily-attendance officials all went for attendance and reported business according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The three provinces and Privy Council followed protocol: before mourning ended, on odd-numbered days the emperor held court at the Welcome-the-Sun Gate; daily-attendance officials offered attendance and reported business as usual.

sentences.zh: 每五日，遇隻日於迎陽門垂簾，皇帝坐於簾內之北，宰執奏事則權屏去左右侍衛；
